TASK: The assembler was seating connector housings into the fixture at final assembly station 6. The task was routine scheduled work. Stage of the task: in process - normal running work. Procedure reference not determined at time of report: the station standard work number is being confirmed by the area lead. The task was being performed as written. Equipment involved: Final assembly fixture at station 6. Equipment state at the time: at rest or stopped. Equipment condition: modified from original. Detail: The fixture was replaced six weeks ago and sits about 4 inches further forward. The object handled weighed under 10 lb. Handling difficulty: small - fits in one hand. It was held pinch grip between fingers and bare handed for feel. PPE in use: safety glasses. This matched the PPE specified for the task.

SEQUENCE: The event was not witnessed and was self reported later. The task is performed several hundred times per shift. The assembler has performed this task for six months to two years. One cycle consists of the following: reach forward about 20 inches into the bin, grasp the housing in a pinch grip, rotate the right wrist to line it up with the fixture, press down with the heel of the hand to seat it, then release and return. Posture held during the task: reaching forward. The task requires moderate force. Symptom onset: Aching and tingling in the right wrist first noticed about eight weeks ago, at first only in the last hour of a shift. Since then the symptoms are affecting grip or function. Recent change in the work: The fixture was replaced about six weeks ago and sits roughly 4 inches further forward, so the reach and the wrist rotation are both greater than before.

MECHANISM: Motion involved: Right wrist rotation of about 90 degrees with the wrist bent back, combined with a downward press using the heel of the hand. It is repeated several hundred times per shift. Each repetition takes moderate force.

CONDITIONS: Difference from a normal run of this task: The fixture change six weeks ago increased the reach and the wrist rotation, and the station has not been reassessed since. Conditions at the point of injury: nothing notable. The event occurred in the second half of the shift. Overtime was being worked that day. It happened within several hours in. The assembler had performed this task before. Whether a known hazard or prior action covers this task was not determined at time of report. No guard, interlock, barrier or control was bypassed, missing, defeated or ineffective. Stop-work opportunity not determined at time of report: there was no single event at which work could have been stopped.

IMMEDIATE ACTIONS: At the scene, no first aid was given at the scene. No first aid was given at the scene. Notified: the team lead and EHS. This happened at the end of the shift. Reason for the delay in reporting: the tingling was mild at first and was expected to settle, and reporting it would have meant stopping the line. Afterwards, nothing was secured. Work at the location continued in a modified way. The assembler was sent to an offsite occupational clinic for evaluation.
